plan.title: Coverage hotspots verb and pre-PR headroom for consumers

narratives.Description: Hairline branch-coverage misses (84.9x vs 85%) force full-suite reruns. Add a consumer-facing coverage:hotspots verb plus pre-PR headroom guidance so agents leave buffer before the expensive global gate. Must deposit via CLI + Taskfile + skill sync — not maintainer-only. This story closes GitHub issue #2683 with a narrowly scoped fix and regression coverage.
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

Recurring hairline branch-coverage fails (84.9x% vs 85% floor) force full `task check` / release Step 5 reruns even when the suite is otherwise green. Same class as #1923, #2135, #2618, #2630, #2666. Policy already rejects an automatic near-miss band (#2573) — keep the hard 85% floor and loud `--allow-coverage-debt=#N` escape hatch. What we lack is **steering tools** so agents leave headroom *before* the expensive global gate.

**Consumer requirement (non-negotiable):** this must ship as a **consumer-facing** surface via published CLI + Taskfile deposit + skill/AGENTS sync — not a maintainer-only script in `deftai/directive`. After `deft update` / deposit, consumer agents get the same cheap coverage loop.

## Problem

1. Global vitest thresholds are fail-closed at 85% branches on all platforms (`vitest.config.ts`). Net-new uncovered `if`/`?:`/`||`/`switch` arms nibble the margin until the next unrelated PR or release trips a hairline miss.
2. Feedback is late: the useful signal only appears at the end of a full coverage run. Agents then guess which modules to patch and rerun the whole suite.
3. Pre-PR / forward-coverage gates do not require local `--coverage` on changed modules or a measured headroom buffer above 85%.
4. Consumers hit the same late-feedback pattern once they run deposited `task check` / pre-PR; a repo-private hotspot helper would not reach them.

## Desired outcome

### A) Published `deft coverage:hotspots` + deposited `task coverage:hotspots`

Deterministic **CLI verb** in `@deftai/directive` (wired through `dispatch` / Taskfile deposit), that from the latest coverage report (or a cheap targeted refresh) prints:

- Current global % for lines / branches / functions / statements vs project thresholds (read from consumer vitest/coverage config when present; fall back to framework default 85%)
- Headroom vs the branch floor (pp)
- Lowest-covered modules under the project's measured source roots
- Uncovered branch/line samples for a caller-supplied path filter (default: git diff vs default branch)

Exit non-zero when global branches are below floor **or** when headroom is below a configured minimum (default suggestion: **0.3pp**), so agents can fail closed *before* opening a PR / cutting a release. Support `--json` for agents.

⊗ Ship only as a script under this monorepo without CLI export + consumer Taskfile wiring.

### B) Pre-PR / always-pin guidance (propagates to consumers)

Teach `deft-directive-pre-pr` (pack source → render → deposit) and a thin AGENTS/commands pointer to:

1. Run targeted coverage on changed modules first (`vitest run --coverage <paths>` / language equivalent), not only full `task check`.
2. Require both sides of new branches (ternary / early-return / catch / default switch / `||` `??`).
3. Treat "barely ≥ floor" as insufficient — aim for ~**≥ floor + 0.3–0.5pp** headroom on the branch metric after the change (floor may be project-specific; do not hardcode only directive's 85% in skill prose).
4. Point at `task coverage:hotspots` / `deft coverage:hotspots` for where to add tests.

Keep dogfood detail in CONTRIBUTING / coding docs; AGENTS stays pointer-thin. Consumers receive this on the next skill/AGENTS refresh after release.

### C) Consumer deposit / sync contract

- [ ] Verb listed in `content/commands.md` and deposited Taskfile namespace consumers already use
- [ ] `deft update` / init-deposit projects the Taskfile target (or documents the `deft coverage:hotspots` CLI path for vendored consumers)
- [ ] Pre-PR skill change is in the skills pack so OpenPackage / `.agents` / `.deft/core` sync paths all see it
- [ ] UPGRADING (or release notes) calls out the new consumer verb + pre-PR habit

## Non-goals

- Lowering the 85% floor in this repo
- Auto-passing Δ < 0.5pp without `--allow-coverage-debt=#N` (#2573 stands)
- Reintroducing a win32-only threshold carve-out
- Replacing attribution via coverage-debt issues when soft-pass is truly needed
- Changing a consumer's chosen coverage floor (USER.md / project policy may be ≥90%); only teach headroom relative to *their* floor
- Maintainer-only scratch tooling that never leaves `deftai/directive`

## Acceptance

- [ ] `deft coverage:hotspots` (and deposited `task coverage:hotspots`) surfaces global metrics, pp headroom, lowest modules, and optional path-filtered uncovered branches
- [ ] Fail-closed when below floor or below configured headroom (default 0.3pp); JSON mode for agents
- [ ] Works in a fresh consumer install after `npm i -g @deftai/directive@…` + `deft update` (or equivalent deposit) — verified by a consumer-path smoke or contract test
- [ ] Pre-PR skill instructs targeted `--coverage` + both-sides branch discipline + headroom aim; AGENTS/commands pointer only
- [ ] Docs state this complements (does not replace) `--allow-coverage-debt=#N` and forward-coverage (#1310)
- [ ] CHANGELOG + regression tests for the verb's parse/report contract
- [ ] UPGRADING / release note mentions consumer availability

## Related

- #2666 (current hairline; may still be open)
- #2573 (coverage-debt escape hatch — do not regress)
- #2630 / #2618 / #2135 / #1923 (prior clearance / boundary flakes)
- #975 (prefer small targeted tests over slow full-suite loops)

## Motivation (operator)

Agents repeatedly burn a full Windows coverage run to discover a 0.02–0.1pp miss. A hotspot+headroom gate turns that into a cheap local loop while preserving the hard floor and attributable soft-pass policy — for **both** directive maintainers and consumers after upgrade.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-07-20T16:19:15Z)

## Amendment (consumer deposit)

Issue body updated so this is **not** maintainer-only tooling:

- Published `deft coverage:hotspots` + deposited `task coverage:hotspots`
- Pre-PR skill / AGENTS pointer via pack render + consumer sync
- Acceptance requires a post-`deft update` consumer-path smoke (or contract test)
- Headroom is relative to the **project** branch floor (may differ from directive's 85%)
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. Implement deft coverage:hotspots CLI module under packages/core + packages/cli dispatch/Taskfile deposit. 2. Report global metrics, pp headroom vs project branch floor, lowest modules, and path-filtered uncovered branches; fail closed below floor or below 0.3pp headroom; support --json. 3. Update deft-directive-pre-pr pack source + render, thin AGENTS/commands pointer, UPGRADING note; verify with unit tests and a consumer-path smoke/contract test; CHANGELOG.
narratives.UserStory: As a directive consumer agent, I want coverage:hotspots and pre-PR headroom guidance after deft update, so that I stop discovering 0.02pp misses only after a full task check.

narrative.Acceptance: deft coverage:hotspots returns global coverage metrics and fails closed when branch headroom is below 0.3pp or below the project floor.
After deft update, deposited task coverage:hotspots and the pre-PR skill emits targeted-coverage plus headroom guidance that displays in the consumer skill file.
Each regression test creates a fixture coverage report and the suite emits passing JSON-contract results; CHANGELOG Unreleased records issue 2683.
